operator: TLScontact, acting for the German Embassy London and Consulate General
allocationMechanism: Short-stay applicants (under 90 days: tourism, medical treatment, family or friends visit, business) cannot book a slot. The applicant registers on TLScontact and enters application details; the application is validated and then placed in a queue; appointments are assigned on a first come, first served basis subject to availability; the applicant is emailed when an appointment is allocated and then has 24 hours to pay the service fee and confirm, and must print the allocation notification for the welcome area. Live at London and Manchester from 1 June 2026 and at Edinburgh from 1 August 2026. The German Embassy calls this a waiting list established to ensure fair and equal access to appointments, and confirms that appointments are allocated automatically. Officially only queue position, slot availability and meeting the 24-hour confirmation window are stated to matter; no official source says registration completeness, contact details or time of registration affects allocation speed. Other visa categories keep the old self-booking system.
representationNote: Unverified. No official page found stating any UK representation arrangement. Applications are as a rule accepted only from UK residents, including holders of a UK Biometric Residence Permit or a UK short-term study visa; non-residents are directed to the German Mission in their country of residence, with exceptions at a visa officer's discretion. Residents of England, Northern Ireland and Wales use London or Manchester; residents of Scotland use Edinburgh.
